subject: Post-call: Model-fit & quantization tradeoffs (AWQ/GPTQ/FP8) \u0004 next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Gupta <samir@finwave.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Model-fit & quantization tradeoffs (AWQ/GPTQ/FP8) - next steps

Hi Samir - great to meet today. Quick recap from our discovery: FinWave needs a model that matches your current document understanding accuracy (~92% entity extraction F1 on your eval set) while cutting inference costs by ~3x relative to your current hosted 70B baseline. Key constraints you mentioned: 150-200ms p50 latency target for single-turn generation on a dedicated GPU pool, and strict data isolation/controls.

What we covered:
- Recommended starting models: Redwood-13B-optimized (intended for 8-bit/4-bit quantization), and Llama-2-70B for a high-accuracy tier.
- Quantization tradeoffs: AWQ and GPTQ give much better throughput than FP16 for smaller models; FP8 shows promise for 70B-class but requires careful calibration.
- Evaluations: you asked for our eval runs on your prompt set + a sample prompt set from you (attached).

Next steps we propose:
1) I'll share a bench summary and a short trade study (attached) that compares AWQ/GPTQ/FP8 across throughput and quality on your representative prompts.
2) Neha will run a short in-house run on the FinWave prompt set to produce a model-fit recommendation (expected by EOD Thu).
3) Dev - can you confirm the networking/KMS questions Samir flagged so we can prepare a Private deployment scoping doc?
4) Samir - can you send the full prompt set and the golden-labels for a ~1k sample? You mentioned procurement will need a mutual action plan to move forward.

Attachments: finwave_prompt_set_v1.json (sample), redwood_benchmark_summary_q2.pdf (preview), awq_vs_gptq_matrix.xlsx (trade matrix).

Thanks - I'll follow up in 48 hours with Neha's initial fit notes.
—Marissa

From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Samir Gupta <samir@finwave.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 07:46:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Post-call: Model-fit & quantization tradeoffs (AWQ/GPTQ/FP8) - Neha's initial fit notes

Hi all - I ran an initial set of evals using the attached prompt sample (finwave_prompt_set_v1.json). Quick highlights:
- Redwood-13B-optimized (AWQ 4-bit) achieves comparable entity extraction F1 to your 70B baseline on the 200-sample subset (delta < 1.5% F1) while improving throughput ~2.8x on our A10x2 test harness.
- GPTQ 4-bit on the 13B also gives good throughput but had a slightly larger quality variance across certain prompt templates (notably long-context questions with nested lists).
- Llama-2-70B with an FP8 profile retains the highest absolute quality but cost per token remains ~2-3x higher vs AWQ-13B; FP8 also required careful per-layer scaling to avoid regression on a handful of prompts.

Attachments: redwood_benchmark_summary_q2.pdf, awq_vs_gptq_matrix.xlsx - the matrix has per-prompt deltas and recommended config knobs.

Concerns/notes:
- We saw a couple of edge-case regressions on list-parsing prompts when aggressively quantizing 13B with GPTQ. I flagged the exact prompt IDs in the matrix.
- For production we recommend a hybrid routing policy: AWQ-quantized 13B as primary for cost/latency, with a fallback to FP8 70B for edge-case, high-value flows. This aligns with Redwood's model routing features and keeps your tail-quality high.

Next operational asks:
- Samir: can you confirm the set of endpoints that must hit the higher-quality fallback (e.g., reconciliation, regulatory extract flows)?
- Dev: I'll need a short host list and permissions to run a 1-day on-prem pilot if you want us to test inside your VPC for accurate latency numbers.

- Neha

Thanks - this is excellent. Procurement (cc'd) will review the benchmark summary and matrix. We'll push the 1k labeled sample to your Drive folder today. A couple asks to close the loop:

If you can get the Private-deploy checklist and the initial MAP by EOD Friday, procurement can start internal approval early next week.

- Samir
